question: If line passing through (3, -1) with slope 4; find y-intercept.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The equation of a straight line in slope-intercept form is given by y = mx + c.

Given the slope m = 4, the equation becomes y = 4x + c.

Substitute the given point (3, -1) into the equation:

⇒ -1 = 4 × 3 + c

⇒ c = -1 − 12 = -13

**∴ The correct answer is -13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Line passes through point (x₁, y₁) = (3, -1)

Slope of the line (m) = 4

**Formula Used:**

Point-slope form of linear equation: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
